options: End their feud and make peace
explanation: To bury the hatchet is an idiomatic expression that means to cease hostilities and reconcile.

text: SECTION D: ORAL ENGLISH (Vowels, Consonants, and Stress). Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the one represented by the underlined letter: f*a*st
explanation: The "a" in "f*a*st" is the long /ɑː/ sound. "Pass" (/pɑːs/) uses the exact same /ɑː/ vowel sound. "Fat" has /æ/, and "pay" has /eɪ/.

text: SECTION D: ORAL ENGLISH (Vowels, Consonants, and Stress). Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the one represented by the underlined letter: c*a*r
explanation: The "a" in "c*a*r" is the long /ɑː/ sound. "Father" (/ˈfɑː.ðər/) also uses the /ɑː/ vowel sound.

text: SECTION D: ORAL ENGLISH (Vowels, Consonants, and Stress). Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the one represented by the underlined letter: c*ome*
explanation: The underlined letters in "c*ome*" produce the short central vowel sound /ʌ/. "Son" (/sʌn/) features the exact same /ʌ/ sound.

text: Choose the correct word with the same vowel sound as the one represented by the underlined letter in clerk.
explanation: In standard Received Pronunciation (RP), clerk is pronounced /klɑːk/. The long vowel /ɑː/ matches the sound in dark (/dɑːk/).

text: Choose the correct option: The opposition party accused the government of ________ the nation's resources.
explanation: "Misappropriating" means dishonestly taking or using funds for one's own use.

text: SECTION D: ORAL ENGLISH (Vowels, Consonants, and Stress). Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the one represented by the underlined letter(s): *ph*one
explanation: The "ph" in "*ph*one" makes the voiceless labiodental fricative sound /f/. "Fan" (/fæn/) shares this exact sound.

text: SECTION D: ORAL ENGLISH (Vowels, Consonants, and Stress). Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the one represented by the underlined letter: *j*ug
explanation: The letter "j" in "*j*ug" produces the voiced postalveolar affricate sound /dʒ/. In "giant" (/ˈdʒaɪ.ənt/), the initial "g" makes the same soft /dʒ/ sound.

text: SECTION D: ORAL ENGLISH (Vowels, Consonants, and Stress). Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the one represented by the underlined letter: *v*oice
explanation: The letter "v" in "*v*oice" produces the voiced labiodental fricative sound /v/. In the word "of" (/ɒv/), the letter "f" is pronounced as the /v/ sound.

text: Choose the correct option: The candidate's answers were completely ________ to the questions asked.
explanation: "Irrelevant" is the standard adjective for not connected to the topic.

text: Choose the word that is most nearly opposite in meaning to *FEEBLE*:
explanation: "Feeble" means weak or lacking strength. "Strong" is its direct opposite.

text: Choose the word that is most nearly opposite in meaning to *TRANSPARENT*:
explanation: "Transparent" means clear or see-through. "Opaque" is its direct opposite.

text: Select the word that contains the voiceless dental fricative /θ/ as in thin.
explanation: Breath (noun) is pronounced /breθ/ with the voiceless dental fricative /θ/. In contrast, smooth, clothes, and breathe (verb) all use the voiced consonant /ð/.

text: SECTION D: ORAL ENGLISH (Vowels, Consonants, and Stress). Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the one represented by the underlined letter: *z*oo
explanation: The letter "z" in "*z*oo" makes the voiced alveolar fricative sound /z/. The initial "x" in "*x*ylophone" (/ˈzaɪ.lə.fəʊn/) is pronounced as /z/.

text: SECTION D: ORAL ENGLISH (Vowels, Consonants, and Stress). Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the one represented by the underlined letter: *g*ame
explanation: The "g" in "*g*ame" represents the hard velar plosive sound /ɡ/. "Goat" (/ɡəʊt/) uses the same /ɡ/ sound, whereas "gem", "giraffe", and "generate" use the soft /dʒ/ sound.

text: Choose the word that is most nearly opposite in meaning to *RIGID*:
explanation: "Rigid" means stiff or unyielding. "Flexible" is its direct opposite.

text: Choose the word that best completes the sentence: The principal's decision was ________ to the smooth running of the school.
explanation: "Conducive" means helpful or favorable to smooth operation.

text: Choose the word that best completes the sentence: The company's decision was ________ to its long-term survival.
explanation: "Critical" means crucial or essential for survival.

text: Choose the word that best completes the sentence: The new evidence was ________ to the case.
explanation: "Crucial" means essential or of great importance to the case.

text: Choose the option that has the correct primary stress placement for the word PHOTOGRAPHY.
explanation: Nouns ending in -graphy place primary stress on the antepenultimate syllable (third from last): /fəˈtɒɡ.rə.fi/. Thus, stress falls on TO.

text: SECTION D: ORAL ENGLISH (Vowels, Consonants, and Stress). Choose the word with the correct stress pattern. IMPORTANT
explanation: "Important" is a three-syllable adjective with primary stress on the second syllable: /ɪmˈpɔː.tənt/.

text: Choose the word that best completes the sentence: The government's policy was ________ to economic growth.
explanation: "Beneficial" means helpful or favorable to economic growth.

text: Select the word that RHYMES with suite.
explanation: Suite is pronounced /swiːt/ and rhymes perfectly with sweet (/swiːt/). Suit is pronounced /suːt/ or /sjuːt/.

text: SECTION D: ORAL ENGLISH (Vowels, Consonants, and Stress). Choose the word with the correct stress pattern. GEOGRAPHY
explanation: Words ending in **-graphy** carry primary stress on the antepenultimate (third from the end) syllable. Thus, stress falls on "OG" (/dʒiˈɒɡ.rə.fi/).

text: Choose the correct option: The director insisted that every staff member ________ the safety training.
explanation: Verbs of insistence ("insisted that...") take the subjunctive mood using base verb (attend).

text: SECTION D: ORAL ENGLISH (Vowels, Consonants, and Stress). Choose the word with the correct stress pattern. DEMOCRACY
explanation: English words ending in **-cracy** carry primary stress on the antepenultimate (third from the end) syllable: /dɪˈmɒk.rə.si/. Thus, stress falls on "MO".

text: Choose the correct option: The manager insisted that the report ________ submitted before the deadline.
explanation: Verbs of insistence ("insisted that...") take the subjunctive mood using base verb (be).

text: Choose the correct option: The panel requested that the documents ________ verified by an expert.
explanation: Verbs of request ("requested that...") take the subjunctive mood using base verb (be).
